texte.091d511cee41: {z1} The rook gives check without a break, for example {z2}. If Black captures it, with the king or the queen, White is stalemated: the pawn on f2 covers g1, the pawn on h3 covers g2, and the pawn on h2 is blocked. If the king steps aside, the next check follows. White only avoids squares where the rook would be captured with check: the first rank (there the queen or the pawn on f2 captures with promotion) and the square b7. All other moves lose, for example {z3} or {z4}. Remember: if your king has no move left, a piece that gives check after check becomes your rescue.

texte.74a814aca384: White threatens {z1}, because the pawns on f7, g7 and h7 take all the squares on the 7th rank from the king, and no black piece can then capture on e8 or interpose on f8. White has already taken precautions with {z6}: if a black rook comes to the first rank with check, the white king has the square h2. Remember: luft costs a pawn move; the back-rank mate costs the game.
texte.025884b330a4: White threatens Re8#, because Black's own pawns block the 7th rank for the black king. Luft such as ...h6 or ...g6, or a blocking move such as ...Ne7, prevents it; White has already taken precautions with h3.

texte.cafe0376c10d: 1. Bb3+! attacks the king on e6, behind which the queen on g8 stands on the same diagonal. The king must move away, and 2. Bxg8 wins the queen.

texte.525cfb75cb8c: Discovered check: {z1} The knight opens the diagonal b3–g8, the bishop gives check, and the knight attacks the queen on h3 at the same time. After {z2}, {z3} or {z4}, {z5} follows. If Black interposes the queen with {z6}, {z7} captures it. {z8} also gives check, even double check, but it leaves the queen alone. Remember: in a discovered check, the moving piece gets a free move. Look for the most valuable target for it.
texte.858aee11ad3d: 1. Nf4+! opens the diagonal of the bishop on b3 with check, and the knight attacks the queen on h3 at the same time. Whatever Black does against the check, White wins the queen; the moving piece picks the most valuable target.
texte.3e0a6c5ae7ed: Decoy and fork: {z1} lures the queen to c8. After {z2}, {z3} and {z4} follow: White gives the rook and wins the queen. If the queen interposes with {z5}, {z6} is mate. texte.c31c34465893: Arabian mate: {z1} (a quiet move) threatens {z2}: the black king has no square (the knight covers g8, the rook covers g7), and Black cannot add a defender to h7, because the pawn on c7 blocks the rook on c8 from reaching the 7th rank. texte.03a93e6d3c41: The quiet move 1. Nf6! threatens 2. Rxh7#: the knight covers g8, the rook covers g7, and Black can no longer defend h7. An unstoppable mate threat is as forcing as a check.
texte.c9e1187061d5: Smothered mate: {z1} (double check by the knight and the queen on c4) {z2} (after {z3}, {z4} is mate) {z5}. The king may not capture the queen, because the knight on h6 covers the square g8. This sequence is called Philidor's legacy. Remember: the queen sacrifice on g8 forces the rook to take the last square from its own king.
texte.91b558413c12: After 1. Nf7+ Kg8 2. Nh6++ Kh8, the queen sacrifice 3. Qg8+!! forces the rook to take the last square from its own king. 4. Nf7# is smothered mate.

texte.229729c86bc4: Removing the defender: apart from the king, only the knight on f6 covers the square h7. {z1} After {z2} or {z3}, {z4} follows (the bishop on d3 defends the queen). texte.d063391e953c: Besides the king, only the knight on f6 covers h7. 1. Rxf6! removes it: after the recapture, 2. Qxh7# is mate; otherwise White stays a piece ahead.
texte.6aa2517d56cd: Queen sacrifice and Anastasia's mate: {z1}. The knight on e7 blocks g6 and g8, and the rook controls the h-file. Remember: when a knight stands on e7, check the sacrifice on h7.
texte.7456f48af9f3: The knight on e7 takes g6 and g8 from the king, so 2. Qxh7+!! opens the h-file for the rook. 3. Rh5# is Anastasia's mate.
texte.6c2b6c61dafa: Boden's mate: {z1}. Black must capture with the pawn, because the king has no square (the bishop on f4 controls b8) and no piece can interpose on c7. Then the bishops' diagonals cross: one gives check on a6 and takes b7 from the king, the other takes c7 and b8. On d7 and d8, Black's own pieces are in the king's way. Remember: if, after queenside castling, only the b-pawn still keeps the diagonal a6–c8 closed, check the sacrifice that draws it away.
texte.61090ddfa8aa: 1. Qxc6+! forces 1... bxc6 and opens the diagonal a6–c8. After 2. Ba6#, the diagonals of the two bishops cross, and the king's own pieces on d7 and d8 cut off its escape.
texte.d554a00bfac0: Damiano's mate: {z1} (or {z2}) {z3}. The rook sacrifice lures the king to h8 (decoy, motif 6): the queen comes to the h-file with check, and the pawn on g6 defends the mating square. texte.48bd6e4e9a6c: The rook sacrifice 1. Rh8+! lures the king to h8, the queen comes to the h-file with check, and 3. Qh7# is mate because g6 defends the mating square. Because every move gives check, Black never gets the chance to capture the queen on d5.
texte.4c157ec9e3e0: Lolli's mate: {z1} threatens {z2}, and Black can no longer defend the square g7, because the bishop that guards it in the fianchetto is missing. Once again a quiet move decides, as in {v1}. Remember: a pawn on f6 and a fianchetto without its bishop together make a mating pattern.
texte.eb91dea92bab: 1. Qh6! threatens 2. Qg7#, and no black bishop defends g7 anymore. A pawn on f6 and a fianchetto without its bishop together make a mating pattern.
